locations.name: Tallowmere
locations.description: Major walled port on the northwestern shore of the central inland sea, built around a sheltered natural harbor where a navigable river reaches the sea. Governed locally by House Denvor under a hereditary charter confirmed by House Kharadorn.

locations.name: Millhaven
locations.description: Grain village and mill center on the River Vale, about 9 miles northwest of Tallowmere. Principal grain collection point supplying the city.

locations.name: Brackenholt
locations.description: Woodland and charcoal settlement west of Tallowmere within the Brackenwood, serving timber, charcoal, and managed woodland trades.

locations.name: Stonehollow
locations.description: Quarry settlement southwest of Tallowmere in the Greyback Ridges, supplying worked stone and quarry labor.

locations.name: Ashcombe Manor
locations.description: Agricultural estate on Ashcombe Rise overlooking the Northfields and northern road.

locations.name: Fordmere
locations.description: Upriver settlement at a dependable crossing of the River Vale, with a chartered crossing administered by House Merewick and a ferry supplement.

locations.name: Saltwick
locations.description: Working shore settlement southeast of Tallowmere with fishing, salt-working, and a modest beacon.

locations.name: Harthbridge
locations.description: Town on the South Road, about 27 miles from Tallowmere, governed under House Velleran's town charter and outside direct Denvor administration.

locations.name: River Vale
locations.description: Principal inland route serving Tallowmere, descending from the western uplands through the farm country and into the harbor.

locations.name: Brackenwood
locations.description: Worked woodland west of Tallowmere supplying fuel, poles, timber, game, and gathered plants.

locations.name: Greyback Ridges
locations.description: Stony hills southwest of Tallowmere, with Stonehollow quarries on accessible eastern faces.

locations.name: Northfields
locations.description: Open agricultural country north and northeast of Tallowmere with farms, orchards, pasture, hedgerows, and drainage hollows.

locations.name: Eastern Shore
locations.description: Irregular shore southeast of Tallowmere with low bluffs, coves, beaches, fishing landings, and salt-working places.

locations.name: Old Stone Bridge
locations.description: Principal permanent river crossing within Tallowmere.

locations.name: Bellwater Pool
locations.description: Deep, slow pool on the River Vale upstream of Millhaven, used by bargemen as a waiting and turning place.

locations.name: Saltwick Beacon
locations.description: Modest shore beacon maintained by Saltwick boat-owning households as a navigation and storm-warning aid.

locations.name: Greywatch Rise
locations.description: Elevated heart of noble authority containing House Denvor's fortified residence, principal garrison buildings, formal gardens, and senior household residences.

locations.name: The High Ward
locations.description: Older, wealthier residential quarter with townhouses, legal offices, established temples, private courtyards, and prosperous families.

locations.name: The Old Quays
locations.description: Old working waterfront with stone warehouses, chandlers, shipwrights, rope-makers, taverns, and established shipping offices.

locations.name: The New Quays
locations.description: Expanded wharves and storage yards serving larger vessels, bulk cargo, bonded warehouses, and newer merchant concerns.

locations.name: Market Ward
locations.description: Commercial center with principal market square, guildhalls, moneychangers, inns, public notices, and specialist shops.

locations.name: Rivergate
locations.description: River-facing district of bargemen, millers, fishmongers, carters, small foundries, tanners, and laborers.

locations.name: Lantern Ward
locations.description: District of shrines, temples, charitable houses, healers, burial grounds, and religious hostels.

locations.name: The Underways
locations.description: Umbrella surface term for accessible subterranean spaces and routes beneath Tallowmere where ratfolk communities live and work. Not one unified settlement or faction.

npcs.name: King Aldric Calderan
npcs.description: Intelligent, educated, patient, politically cautious, and increasingly frustrated by the limits placed on the Crown.

npcs.name: Lord Theren Vaelorian
npcs.description: Cultured, patient, calculating, and difficult to surprise. Prefers financial and diplomatic leverage to direct threats.

npcs.name: High King Durnak Kharadorn
npcs.description: Stern, disciplined, traditional, and deeply conscious of his family history.

npcs.name: Lord Garrick Edarth
npcs.description: Traditional martial lord who values discipline, loyalty, and reputation.

npcs.name: Lord Edran Veyr
npcs.description: Practical and reserved, accustomed to difficult decisions with limited resources.

npcs.name: Lady Maris Merrowen
npcs.description: Accomplished political operator with extensive commercial and diplomatic relationships.

npcs.name: Lord Oswin Denvor
npcs.description: Measured and observant, preferring negotiated solutions and predictable obligations.

npcs.name: Lady Catrin Denvor
npcs.description: Politically capable Denvor household member who maintains civic and charitable relationships.

npcs.name: Ser Edwyn Denvor
npcs.description: Recognized heir who favors greater investment in defenses and infrastructure.

npcs.name: Lady Anwen Denvor
npcs.description: Perceptive and socially skilled, with genuine relationships outside the nobility.

npcs.name: Reeve Marrec Holt
npcs.description: Methodical and protective of administrative records; values dependable civic routines.

npcs.name: Harbor Master Ysella Vane
npcs.description: Direct, experienced, and difficult to intimidate. Wants safe traffic and fair quay allocation.

npcs.name: Chief Magistrate Odran Pell
npcs.description: Patient, observant, and exacting about testimony.

npcs.name: Captain Brinna Salk
npcs.description: Practical and blunt, with strong responsibility toward her patrols.

npcs.name: Castellan Hadrik Voss
npcs.description: Veteran professional who values preparation, stores, and clear command.

npcs.name: Meret Sorn
npcs.description: Polished and cautious. Values predictable trade, secure cargo, fire prevention, and reliable records.

npcs.name: Dagna Coppervein
npcs.description: Exacting craftswoman who protects apprentices, skilled labor, quality standards, and timber supply.

npcs.name: Pellan Reed
npcs.description: Sociable, sharp, and politically perceptive. Wants fair river tolls and safe landings.

npcs.name: Tavren Selwick
npcs.description: Prosperous merchant known for paying obligations and keeping accurate cargo accounts.

npcs.name: Nix-of-the-Cistern
npcs.description: Patient and attentive to practical needs. A local contact, not a representative of all ratfolk.

npcs.name: Tikka Vell
npcs.description: Resourceful and commercially ambitious. Wants ratfolk workshops to sell openly in the Market Ward.

npcs.name: Serren Coil
npcs.description: Quiet and observant, protective of route knowledge and family shelters.

npcs.name: Miraq Ashwhisk
npcs.description: Capable independent craftswoman with a respected surface business.

npcs.name: Sister Alwen
npcs.description: Calm, stubborn, and practical. Wants food, shelter, care, burial assistance, and support for abandoned children.

npcs.name: Brother Caldus
npcs.description: Thoughtful listener who records names of the missing and lost and values maritime rites.

npcs.name: Noll Tarrow
npcs.description: Former tally clerk organizing the loose Grey Net cargo-diversion network in the Old Quays.

npcs.name: Edrik Vale
npcs.description: Copyist and occasional contract clerk who produces altered commercial documents and false ownership papers.

npcs.name: Hessa Quill
npcs.description: Former household steward who arranges private loans and coercive settlements.

npcs.name: Sella Vane
npcs.description: Independent boat owner who moves small quantities of undeclared goods through minor quays and river landings.

npcs.name: Othric Pell
npcs.description: Trades schedules, overheard conversations, debt rumors, and introductions. Not omniscient.

npcs.name: Dannel Rusk
npcs.description: Independent private debt enforcer who works for multiple creditors and sometimes pushes beyond lawful agreements.

npcs.name: Prelate Damas Orrel
npcs.description: Careful administrator of the Open Ledger who emphasizes lawful trade, contracts, civic order, and fair procedure.

npcs.name: Keeper Lethia Sorn
npcs.description: Reserved and compassionate priest of the Quiet Gate who insists the dead be treated with dignity.

npcs.name: Lord Chancellor Othmar Rusk
npcs.description: Crown administrator and appointed Imperial Council representative with access to royal government and inter-house negotiation.

npcs.name: Lady Meredyth Sorn
npcs.description: Precise Crown financial administrator concerned about short-term borrowing and privileges granted to powerful houses.

npcs.name: Lord Bastian Wycliffe
npcs.description: Learned jurist cautious about changing law by decree and attentive to royal precedent and noble privilege.

npcs.name: Marshal Garran Holt
npcs.description: Career soldier who understands the Crown's military limitations and favors a more reliable royal force.

npcs.name: Mistress Nerys Vale
npcs.description: Discreet intelligence officer whose network relies on informants, servants, merchants, messengers, and intermediaries.

npcs.name: Lord Perrin Ashcombe
npcs.description: Courtier responsible for royal household operations, ceremony, schedules, palace staff, and access to the monarch.

npcs.name: Lady Mereth Relland
npcs.description: Careful and proud head of the minor house, concerned with preserving family standing and its official account of the old South Road incident.

npcs.name: Ser Corren Relland
npcs.description: Adult heir focused on restoring House Relland's income and local reputation. His knowledge of the old incident is incomplete.

npcs.name: Lord Edvar Relland
npcs.description: Deceased former head of House Relland who controlled the household response to the old South Road incident.

npcs.name: Ser Deylan Marrick
npcs.description: Former road-patrol leader who abused his authority while operating under House Relland colors. He died during the South Road incident.

houses.name: House Calderan
houses.description: The ruling dynasty and Crown. Its post-Rebellion authority is substantial but constrained by the political settlement and Imperial Council.

houses.name: House Vaelorian
houses.description: Elven Great House of the western highlands. Maintains financial dominance and trade access through diplomacy and leverage.

houses.name: House Kharadorn
houses.description: Dwarven Great House and empire. Seeks independence, control of the inland sea and Dragonstone, and freedom from surface interference in clan affairs.

houses.name: House Edarth
houses.description: Human Great House of the western heartlands. Values traditional noble rights, military and agricultural strength, and resistance to excessive royal centralization.

houses.name: House Veyr
houses.description: Human Great House of the northern marches. Focused on frontier security, resources for the Northern Watch, and preserving control of the north.

houses.name: House Merrowen
houses.description: Human Great House of the eastern coast. Protects eastern ports and shipping, commercial independence, and maritime influence.

houses.name: House Denvor
houses.heraldry_description: A black heron standing in shallow silver water upon a deep green field.
houses.description: Established minor human house ruling Tallowmere from Greywatch under a hereditary charter confirmed by House Kharadorn. Locally powerful but not a Great House.

houses.name: House Relland
houses.description: Minor human noble house with a modest manor and tenant holdings along the South Road within broader House Velleran-chartered lands. House Relland bears institutional responsibility for the unlawful conduct of its retainers and subsequent cover-up in the South Road Merchant Incident.

factions.name: Harbor Fellowship
factions.description: Shipowners and maritime interests concerned with berth access, harbor operations, and commercial predictability.

factions.name: Warehouse Guild
factions.description: Recognized warehouse operators and factors concerned with secure cargo, records, fire prevention, and access.

factions.name: Market Guild
factions.description: Established market members and merchants concerned with stalls, commercial access, and trade privileges.

factions.name: River Carters' and Bargemen's Company
factions.description: River operators seeking fair tolls, safe landings, and recognition for inland transport.

factions.name: Shipwrights' Brotherhood
factions.description: Skilled shipwright organization protecting apprentices, craft standards, labor, and timber supply.

factions.name: Ratfolk Underways Community
factions.description: Decentralized ratfolk community beneath Tallowmere with families, workshops, routes, and limited coordination. It is not a unified criminal faction or single political bloc.

factions.name: The Grey Net
factions.description: Loose arrangement of handlers, carters, lookouts, and buyers involved in cargo diversion, dockside theft, false handling claims, and resale.

factions.name: The Bent Seal
factions.description: Loose fraud network dealing in forged cargo marks, altered receipts, false ownership papers, and commercial fraud.

factions.name: The Quiet Account
factions.description: Informal network arranging private lending, debt collection, coercion, and settlements.

factions.name: Artificers' Hall
factions.description: Recognized masters in metalwork, carpentry, leatherwork, pottery, textiles, and related crafts.

quests.name: Roadside Troll Attack
quests.summary: A Selwick & Company wagon carrying ordinary commercial cargo is attacked by a troll on the PCs' approach to Tallowmere. Protecting the crew or recovering the consignment can earn a modest reward and a written introduction to Meret Sorn.

quests.name: Warehouse Guild Introduction
quests.summary: A signed recommendation from Tavren Selwick can provide the PCs a first commercial meeting with Meret Sorn. It grants credibility, not guild membership or universal trust.
